title: ReInk: A Training-Free Inference Wrapper for Robust Chart Question Answering Under Visual Degradations

contributions.purpose: Improve VLM robustness on visually corrupted charts without any model training.
contributions.mechanism: ReInk, a training-free inference wrapper that runs off-the-shelf OCR (EasyOCR) on the corrupted chart and renders the extracted text at its original bounding-box locations on a clean canvas, then feeds both the corrupted chart and the re-inked canvas to a multi-image VLM (Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct).
contributions.evaluation: On ChartQAPro-Corrupted, ReInk reaches 27.95% overall accuracy vs 15.74% baseline (+12.21pp).
contributions.domain: Chart question answering under visual corruption (VLM robustness)
contributions.source_quote: We propose ReInk, a training-free inference wrapper that improves VLM robustness on corrupted charts by providing OCR-extracted text as a spatially-rendered auxiliary image.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrate that gains come from correct text semantics rather than layout cues.
contributions.mechanism: Comprehensive experiments on ChartQAPro-Corrupted including a scrambled-text control (B) that preserves bounding-box layout but permutes text strings across boxes.
contributions.evaluation: ReInk gives +12.21pp over baseline (27.95% vs 15.74%) and +8.50pp over the scrambled-text control (27.95% vs 19.45%).
contributions.domain: Chart question answering under visual corruption (VLM robustness)
contributions.source_quote: We conduct comprehensive experiments on ChartQAPro-Corrupted, demonstrating +12.21pp improvement over baseline and +8.50pp over a scrambled-text control, confirming that correct text semantics drive the gains.

contributions.purpose: Determine which components of ReInk actually matter.
contributions.mechanism: Ablation study comparing spatially-rendered canvas vs OCR-as-text-in-prompt, and removing bounding-box outlines, plus a clean-chart sanity check.
contributions.evaluation: Text content is the primary driver (+11.57pp from OCR text alone); spatial rendering adds only +0.64pp and bounding-box outlines only +0.10pp; clean-chart benefit is negligible (+0.13pp).
contributions.domain: Chart question answering under visual corruption (VLM robustness)
contributions.source_quote: We analyze what components matter: text content is the primary driver (+11.57pp from OCR text alone), while spatial rendering (+0.64pp) and bounding box outlines (+0.10pp) provide marginal additional benefit.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Unlike these approaches that require training or architectural modifications, ReInk operates as a training-free inference wrapper that provides OCR-extracted text as a complementary visual input.

In the chart domain, DePlot (Liu et al., 2022) converts charts to tables using OCR, enabling one-shot reasoning with language models. UniChart (Masry et al., 2023) and ChartMoE (Xu et al., 2024) incorporate chart-specific pretraining, while Dragonfly (Thapa et al., 2024) uses multi-resolution encoding to capture fine-grained details.

To assess robustness, we create ChartQAPro-Corrupted by applying two corruption types at severity level 4 (major): defocus blur and pixelate, following the ImageNet-C protocol (Hendrycks & Dietterich, 2019).

notes: OCR-as-text in the prompt nearly matches the proposed spatial rendering (-0.64pp), i.e. the paper's own headline spatial-rendering mechanism provides only marginal benefit over a trivial text-injection baseline; ReInk also hurts 4.72% of questions (trade-off).
